messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Subject: Performance MAP: Throughput benchmarking plan + unit economics

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is the draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with the performance evaluation milestones we discussed. The immediate objective for this week is to validate sustained throughput and per-request unit economics under representative traffic, so we can finalize the recommended serving configuration for your production rollout.

High-level ask:
- Provide a sample workload (200–500 representative requests or synthetic generator) and a CSV of token distributions per request.
- Confirm target concurrency/peak window (you mentioned a 60-minute synchronous batch around settlements).

Evaluation plan (summary):
- Metrics: tokens/sec (sustained), requests/sec (sustained QPS), TTFT (time-to-first-token), median & 99th pct latency, throughput at concurrency targets.
- Model variants to test: redwood-7b-q4, redwood-13b-fp16, redwood-70b-8bit (for capacity planning).
- Conditions: cold start vs warm (KV cache primed), batching sweeps (batch sizes 1/4/8/16), concurrency sweep (4/8/16/32).
- Deliverables: CSV of raw times per request, CSV summary (throughput, latencies), unit-econ PDF (cost per 1M tokens + cost per 100k requests), and a short slide with recommended config for production.

Proposed timeline (MAP milestones):
- 03/02: FinTechCo shares sample workload and test account (API key + test dataset).
- 03/03–03/04: Redwood runs benchmarks and iterates on batch/concurrency knobs.
- 03/05: Deliver results + unit econ; joint review call and decide target model + reserved capacity sizing.

Can you confirm the sample workload availability and whether we should run tests in your us-west region or Redwood-hosted test region?

Attaching: 20260301-map-draft.xlsx (draft MAP with milestone owners).

Cheers,
Sergio
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Sergio/Laura —

Plan for the benchmark harness (I'll run on a dedicated test pool):
- Synthetic driver: replay 300 requests (FinTechCo sample) at fixed RPS until 60 minutes or until 95% of budget used.
- Warm vs cold: cold = fresh worker pool; warm = pre-warm with 5 full passes over dataset.
- Measurements collected: requests/sec (sustained), tokens/sec (aggregate), median/95/99p latency for first-token and completion, memory/GPU util, and KV cache hit-rate.

Configuration matrix (examples we will run):
- redwood-7b-q4: batch sizes [4,8,16], conc [8,16,32]
- redwood-13b-fp16: batch sizes [1,4,8], conc [4,8,16]
- redwood-70b-8bit: batch sizes [1,2,4], conc [2,4,8]

Preliminary expected ballpark (estimate before run):
- redwood-7b-q4: sustained 120 req/s at avg 140 tokens/request => tokens/sec ~16800; median TTFT ~140ms warm, 480ms cold; 99p completion ~310ms
- redwood-13b-fp16: sustained 40–55 req/s => tokens/sec ~5600–7700; median TTFT ~220ms warm, 920ms cold; 99p completion ~420–650ms
- redwood-70b-8bit: sustained 8–14 req/s => tokens/sec ~960–1680; median TTFT ~420ms warm, 1600ms cold; 99p completion >1200ms

Unit economics assumptions (on-demand):
- compute $/hr translated to $/1M tokens (projection) — will attach final numbers after run, but expect cost ranking: 7b-q4 << 13b-fp16 << 70b-8bit.

I'll run the matrix on 03/04 and attach raw exports + a summarized CSV.

-Priyom
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance MAP: Throughput benchmarking plan + unit economics — results attached

Hi all —

Attached are the raw results (throughput-results-0305.csv) and the unit economics summary (unit-econ-summary-0305.pdf). Highlights below (warm runs, sustained 60-minute window, 120 tokens/request average):

1) redwood-7b-q4
- Best steady config: batch=16, concurrency=32
- Sustained RPS: 110 req/s
- Tokens/sec: 13,200 tokens/sec
- Median TTFT: 130ms (warm), Cold TTFT median 460ms
- 99p completion latency: 310ms
- Estimated cost: $4.6 per 1M tokens (on-demand); reserved projection: $2.1 per 1M tokens

2) redwood-13b-fp16
- Best steady config: batch=8, concurrency=16
- Sustained RPS: 46 req/s
- Tokens/sec: 5,520 tokens/sec
- Median TTFT: 210ms (warm), Cold TTFT median 940ms
- 99p completion latency: 560ms
- Estimated cost: $12.2 per 1M tokens (on-demand); reserved projection: $6.3 per 1M tokens

3) redwood-70b-8bit
- Best steady config: batch=2, concurrency=4
- Sustained RPS: 10 req/s
- Tokens/sec: 1,200 tokens/sec
- Median TTFT: 410ms (warm), Cold TTFT median 1,750ms
- 99p completion latency: 1,310ms
- Estimated cost: $38.4 per 1M tokens (on-demand); reserved projection: $19.0 per 1M tokens

Notes/observations:
- 7b-q4 gives the best unit economics for their typical request size; it comfortably meets the 60-concurrency burst target with margin.
- 13b-fp16 provides a quality/latency tradeoff and may be appropriate for enrichment pipelines where higher model capability is required; cost per token ~2.6x vs 7b-q4.
- 70b-8bit is expensive and only recommended for small fractions of traffic (e.g., high-sensitivity reconciliation scoring) or as a fallback.

I've attached the CSV with per-request timestamps and the PDF with cost assumptions and math. Happy to walk through numbers on the joint call.

Best,
Priyom
